steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Roll dough into 1-inch balls and bake for 15 minutes in the oven.
Once baked, roll while still hot in confectioners' sugar until coated. Let cool. Lightly dust with more confectioners' sugar.

raw_recipe.headline: Emma's Russian Tea Cakes
raw_recipe.description: These easy tea cakes are delectable Russian cookies made with walnuts and rolled in confectioners' sugar. These treats are perfect for parties.
raw_recipe.name: Emma's Russian Tea Cakes

review.reviewBody: I've made these every year for Christmas ever since I was a teenager. They are so delicious and look beautiful on a cookie tray. My suggestions are that you will need more powdered sugar than stated. Put a few of the hot cookies at a time into a paper bag with the sugar in, shake gently to coat, remove and set aside on a rack to cool. The first coating with sugar will get soft from the heat, then when they are completely cooled, coat again and the sugar will adhere to the first coating making the outside nice and white.

My husband said these were just like the 'Russian Tea Balls' his mother used to make. I creamed the butter and sugar together before adding the other ingredients. I used closer to 1 cup of chopped walnuts, no salt and did not chill the batter. After taking them out of the oven, I rolled them in powdered sugar and dusted with more after they cooled. Delicious!

I live at high altitude in a very dry climate, and had to add 2 Tbsp. cold water to the dough. Don't overwork the dough - it's ok if it's crumbly and you have to press the balls together so they'll hold their shape. The resulting cookies will be delicate and fall apart in your mouth rather than being tough. For me, these were a taste of childhood and brought back memories of baking with my mother.

I love these cookies! I use toasted coconut instead of nuts and they turned out great! Also make sure you mix the butter and sugar together first before adding the rest of the ingredients. There also is no need to refridgerate before rolling into balls and cooking. An easier way to make into balls is to use a very small icecream scoop, its a time saver!

I like this recipe. It's the one in the Betty Crocker Cooky Book that my grandma made every year. I love this recipe with salted butter. But I have the hardest time with this recipe in that the dough is too crumbly. I use a cookie scooper and press the dough into it to shape. I make a double batch usually. My hands hurt at the end, but my labors are rewarded. These are wonderful to share with doctors' offices. And these are my mom's favorite cookies. I did do some research. Many said to add more butter. I could try to chill for less time or not at all. Form the dough into a rectangle and wrap it in Saran wrap. I could add 1 tablespoon of milk if it's too crumbly. I did wonder if it's the 1/4 cup of flour. Let me know if anyone has tried this without that extra 1/4 cup and had less crumbly dough.

Delicious! I substituted the walnuts with 1/2 a cup of roughly chopped dark chocolate. I found i didn't need to chill the dough and baked them for 13minutes. The second time i made them i substitued the butter for reduced fat margarine and they still turned out the same.

My mother had a similar recipe. She called them Snowballs & we still make them every Christmas. The only difference is that we use almonds instead of walnuts & almond flavoring instead of vanilla. We make them small enough to be one bite because delicious as they are, they tend to be messy to bite into, so it's important to watch the baking time. I agree with other readers that the sugar & butter need to be creamed until fluffy before adding the other ingredients.

To the lady that was confused on the crumbly dough...it rolls right up and sticks together great, with no added liquid. It just doesn't appear that way at first bease it's so crumbly. Also, I added 3 TBS Extra of confectioners powdered sugar, & 1/2 tsp more of Vanilla. ;-) Made them with/without pecans. ;-) Baked them for (20) minutes instead.They were great!! Very Tasty. Great for parties or special occasions. Not just Christmas. ;-)

This is the closest to what my great grandmother made! Sadly we lost all of our recipes when we were robbed,I know who steals a cook book,and had been on the hunt for YEARS to find something even close.
We do two things different.We "burn" the butter,really you're browning the salt when it melts,and let it set back up.Also we put powdered sugar in a large bowl,add done cookies and gently roll them around.


I've had folks PAY me to make these for them that's how good they are!

Emma, good job hunting this recipe! These cookies are in fact THE ORIGINAL Russian Teacakes. I have a hand written copy in my hand as we speak. Here's the way the "holy grail" (hahahaha!)has been handed down all these years to me: 1. Don't over chill them. About thirty minutes is good. 2. Don't make them too big. These are supposed to be dainty cookies. 3. These cookies don't spread, so you can add a few more than normal. Also, unless you have a convection oven, don't try to put more than one sheet in your oven. 4. Bake these cookies until they are just barely turning golden on the bottom, because they will continue to cook on the sheet. These cookies should be "tender", and melt in your mouth. Not crunchy. 5. Because you have left them till they are just barely golden on the bottom, do not, repeat, do not move them from the sheet until they are almost completely cool, or they will fall apart. 6. This is the tricky part. You need to roll? toss? dust? them in the powdered sugar without busting them. I was shown to do it in a bowl about half full of podered sugar, one at a time, cradling them in my fingers, back and forth. (I know, sounds crazy!) Ok, I'll stop yacking now! Again, thanks for posting THE ORIGINAL recipe!

These are wonderful! I had a recipe a while ago from some Polish friends and lost it! This is the much the same as I can recall. However I didn't use the walnuts( they aren't my first choice) I used toasted pecans! Yummmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmm!!! So good. This is a very easy recipe! I know people said that some of the steps are left out but it's pretty easy none the less. Also I rolled in 10x as soon as they came out of the oven! Then I let them cool and rolled them again. Thank you very much for sharing this recipe!
I never can make too many of these cookies. Best ever. Bakery cookies just don’t compare. This Christmas I have made over 300 of them.
I love it. I used pecans.
I made these for a get together and all my friends loved them
Great recipe! I used pistachios in one batch and pecans in the next. Next will be walnuts. Everyone loved them - me especially.
Absolutely love these! Will share picture soon.
I changed it up and used a cinnamon-sugar dusting instead of more powdered sugar. My family liked them.
Very easy delicious little cakes
Russian Tea Cakes were not a cookie my Mother ever made, but I had a friend whose Mother made them at the holidays and I loved them as a child. This has become a holiday staple for us.
Easiest cookie I’ve ever made! I thought the bakery purchased ones were good.... not even close to these. Next time I’ll make more.
